text: {"findings":[{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days and no MDE/power","detail":"A 1-week run is below the 14-day minimum standard, and storms are intermittent so exposure may be tiny. No MDE, sample size, or power calculation is given.","evidence_quote":"Run for 1 week. Compare on-time rate between arms.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Run at least 14 days (likely longer to capture enough storm events), and specify MDE, power, and required storm-delivery sample size."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for promise window change","detail":"Widening promise windows affects customer experience and delivery speed, but only Cost Per Delivery is guarded. Guardrails such as customer satisfaction/CSAT, contact rate or cancellation rate, and promise accuracy/delivery speed are absent.","evidence_quote":"Cost Per Delivery: must not increase.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as CSAT, customer contact rate, order cancellation rate, and average promised vs. actual delivery time/conversion."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Baseline stated without verifiable source","detail":"The 78% baseline is stated as fact without a source; the only source cited is a generic weather impact analysis for the problem statement, not for this figure.","evidence_quote":"baseline 78%, target 88% within 8 weeks","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the data source, query, and time period for the 78% baseline."},{"type":"PRIOR_ART","title":"Prior experiment referenced without learnings","detail":"The proposal says it follows EXP-014 but does not state what EXP-014 found or how this design addresses those results.","evidence_quote":"Follows EXP-014, but only applies during storms rather than permanently.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Summarize EXP-014's outcome (e.g., impact on on-time rate, conversion, cost) and explain how it informs this design."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Randomization by customer may leak between arms","detail":"Storms are geographically correlated and drivers/routes serve customers in both arms, so customer-level randomization can cause interference (shared capacity, routing) and contamination of the on-time comparison.","evidence_quote":"A/B test randomized by customer.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Randomize at a geographic or delivery-zone/store level (e.g., switchback or cluster randomization) to avoid spillover."}]}
